title: Study of G-CSF for DOR in Patients Undergoing IVF
official: Research Protocol for a Double-Blinded Randomized Trial of Granulocyte Colony Stimulating Factor (G-CSF) for Treatment of Diminished Ovarian Reserve in Patients Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)
summary:
Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is defined by reduced follicle counts in women, associated with decreased fertility and lower success rates with In Vitro Fertilization (IVF). Granulocyte Colony Stimulating Factor (G-CSF) is a medication that has been proposed as a potential treatment for DOR, as it may help to improve ovarian function and increase the number of mature eggs available for fertilization. However, the efficacy and safety of G-CSF for DOR in IVF patients have not been definitively established. Therefore, our research protocol aims to assess the effectiveness of G-CSF in improving IVF outcomes in patients with DOR in POSEIDON group 4 (age ≥35 years and AMH \<1.2 ng/mL).

In this double-blinded randomized controlled trial, 140 participants with DOR will receive subcutaneously 5 single doses of 300 μg of G-CSF (Neupogen, study group) or saline solution (placebo, control group), administered as one injection every other day starting in early luteal phase and for a total of 10 days, during standard IVF priming. All participants will undergo ovarian stimulation for IVF in the subsequent menstrual cycle following CHR's clinical protocols.

The primary outcomes will be the total number of eggs and of mature eggs retrieved. Secondary outcomes will include maturation, fertilization, viable day 3 or day 5 high quality embryos and clinical pregnancies, as well as collecting safety data.

Findings of this study may help to clarify the effect of G-CSF on ovarian function and IVF outcomes in women with DOR.

interventions.name: Subcutaneous injections of a saline solution

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Infertile women aged 35-44 years who have indication to undergo IVF and meet the POSEIDON group 4 (DOR): FSH \<10 IU/L and AMH \>1.2 ng/mL
* Participants will be recruited from patients undergoing IVF treatment at The CHR
